homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'EPC' is the census's short name (aka) and the center's own; as a bare acronym it names other entities (none on the rail, none in T). 'epc.buffalo.edu' is its former address (aka). The distinct entities below are named by the field, the census or the archive beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: PennSound (writing.upenn.edu/pennsound/), its sister site at CPCW, Penn, the audio archive (B6; F46; LS-26): a census row of its own (pennsound)
UbuWeb (ubu.com), its partner (B7; F21; LS-30): a census row of its own (ubuweb)
Jacket2, whose tributes its memorial entries link (LS-31): a census row of its own (jacket2)
the Center for Programs in Contemporary Writing (CPCW) at the University of Pennsylvania, its collaborator and publisher (F46, F39), an institution distinct from the center
the Poetics Program at SUNY-Buffalo (founded 1991, F19) and the Poetics List (1993–2014, F45): a program and a listserv whose archives the center houses, distinct from it
the ELMCIP Knowledge Base (B3), which records the center, and the Electronic Literature Foundation, named beside Glazier in #301 (O301-02): distinct entities
the Electronic Literature Lab (a census row of its own, electronic-literature-lab): a distinct entity with a near name

captures.description: THE CENTER, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'The Electronic Poetry Center is a major online archive and resource gateway for digital, experimental, and avant-garde poetry.' Overview & History (founded 'July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein'; the Poetics Program at SUNY Buffalo; E-Poetry 2001); Key Resources & Features (author libraries; the E-Poetry section; partnerships with PennSound and UbuWeb). Four cards: the center at the University of Pennsylvania, Wikipedia, the ELMCIP Knowledge Base, poets.org.

atoms.evidence: Overview: Electronic Poetry Center (EPC) is an online resource for digital poetry
Founded: July 10, 1994, by Loss Pequeño Glazier and Charles Bernstein.
is a major online archive and resource gateway for digital, experimental, and avant-garde poetry.
Author Libraries: Curated collections of contemporary poet pages containing biographies, photos, essays, and links to online works.
Origin: Created as part of the Poetics Program at the State University of New York (SUNY) at Buffalo.
